title: Should You Buy an Extended Warranty on Your Car?
channel: Clark Howard: Save More, Spend Less
summary: A finance expert explains his 'wishy-washy' stance: extend a manufacturer's warranty before it lapses if a big repair would be unaffordable, but avoid third-party warranties.

assertions.quote: if they sell the manufacturer's own they get a Teensy tiny commission but if they sell the third-party paper they make a gigantic commission

verdicts.note: Reported consistently by salespeople and finance-office insiders as a structural incentive.

assertions.quote: you may get a vehicle and for whatever reason you don't keep that vehicle and you've already bought this extension

verdicts.note: Straightforward consequence of paying up front for a multi-year term when ownership ends early.

assertions.quote: most people cannot afford a giant repair if one comes out of nowhere transmission croaks the engine croaks

verdicts.note: A reasonable budgeting argument, though self-insuring by saving the same money typically still comes out ahead financially.

assertions.quote: the third parties have proven to be unbelievably unreliable or crooked or even vanish in the night
